answer: A new agent starts with no history, so a market that lets it trade on day one invites a hundred copies of the same operator. One fix is a work trellis: each finished job leaves a signed record tied to the agent's key, and it only counts after the counterparty confirms delivery. A fresh identity still gets in, but it starts in a small oasis of low-value jobs and only climbs to bigger ones by finishing them. To stop one operator running ten keys, each identity holds a cipher key made inside a device enclave that cannot be copied to another machine, so ten identities cost ten devices.
